_comment: C6-5 genmo bodies EN. 无附加小节。正文「相关条目」3 行带 .md 链接（runway/luma/flux），related 写 3 条。sources 4 条对齐 frontmatter。

axes.model_access: In-house model line + open weights: Mochi 1, an open-source text-to-video model (GitHub genmoai/mochi, Apache-2.0, 3,757 stars, pushed 2026-10-22, GitHub API verified the same day); the in-product model-selection surface sits behind a login wall, and the exact tier follows the signed-in UI.
axes.runtime: Web (genmo.ai, /playground 200); product generation on the vendor's cloud. Open weights + training/inference code can run locally (provided in the repo) — self-running is a repo-level fact; the product itself ships no offline client.
axes.local_files: Product works are stored account-side in the cloud; open weights plus training/inference code go local once downloaded (Apache-2.0). The product ships no offline client — self-running is the Mochi repo surface, not in-product inference.
axes.background: A product generation request queues on the vendor cloud, with waiting time varying by tier and queue; the product surface has no pause, resume or task-position control. Local Mochi inference is managed by the user's own process and stops when the machine shuts down.
axes.tools: Text-to-video (the Mochi 1 line); the homepage headlines the "Open world models" narrative; /docs and /api both 307 into a login wall, so public product documentation is limited and editing/interaction follows the playground UI.
axes.context: Works are organised by account; the product surface has no cross-session memory entry. Reusable Mochi weights and code are asset reuse, not conversation context or persistent memory.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription system (/pricing 200, D9: prices not collected); the training-use switch sits in account settings, with the exact path following the signed-in UI; training/commercial freedom of the open-weights repo follows Apache-2.0 itself.
axes.fit: Fits: creators and researchers who want open weights to self-run (Apache-2.0 is a rare permissive tier in this category), world-model narrative tracking, creative experiments. Does not fit: mainland compliance scenarios (not serving the mainland), enterprise SLA as the headline (no SLA commitment on the public page).
